problem: Characterize the higher-dimensional good strict non-Archimedean analytic spaces on which every classically plurisubharmonic function is locally a decreasing limit of semipositive real piecewise-linear functions. This is P02.1 of the monograph's current active inventory, the first of four separate regularization targets. Do not replace it by locally Fubini--Study, weakly smooth, or ordinary CLD-smooth approximation. State the complete base-field, scalar-extension, dimension, separation, boundary, singularity and coefficient hypotheses of any proposed characterization. Classical psh means upper semicontinuous u:X -> R union {-infinity} such that after every analytic extension K'/K, every pullback to a connected smooth strict K'-analytic curve is subharmonic in the Thuillier sense. Semipositive real PL means the real-PL positivity notion of Gubler--Rabinoff used in the book, not arbitrary piecewise-affine convexity on one selected skeleton. The local statement must give one fixed ordinary neighbourhood of each point and a pointwise decreasing sequence on that neighbourhood; a varying-domain construction or a net without a justified countable reduction is insufficient. The extended-valued and scalar-extension cases must be retained or explicitly excluded as an essential hypothesis. Known background: continuous invariant current-psh functions on split-toric tropical domains already have local decreasing semipositive real-PL approximants under the good-strict hypothesis. Curves and real-PL positivity comparison are also known scoped cases. Reproving only that invariant subfamily does not characterize all classical psh functions. Earlier routes fail at compatible gluing of curvewise approximants, positivity on overlapping tropical charts, or unsupported replacement of nets by sequences. Develop new arguments, seek obstructions and counterexamples, and record failed routes and any strictly scoped partial result honestly.
completionCriteria: Provide a precise necessary-and-sufficient geometric or analytic criterion with a complete proof of both directions, covering arbitrary classically psh functions in the stated higher-dimensional category rather than only torus-invariant continuous functions. The criterion must be independently checkable and must not merely restate the requested approximation property, assume the unresolved regularization input, or identify generated CLD psh with curve-test psh without proof. Justify every source-dependent input in its exact primary-source scope, every limiting operation, local fixed-domain compatibility, and all singular, boundary, scalar-extension and -infinity cases used. Test the characterization on curves, split tori, smooth polydiscs, noninvariant functions, singular and nonnormal spaces where meaningful. A useful partial theorem, conditional reduction, failed proof, or obstruction to a stronger universal claim should be retained as research notes but does not complete this exact classification task. Final acceptance requires requirements checking and independent reconstruction of the candidate and every generated supporting claim; repository source/receipt and integration gates remain separate.
